moistureRecyclingCascade.title: The rain a forest makes for itself
moistureRecyclingCascade.subtitle: Follow one column of air inland and watch how much of the rain has already fallen once.
moistureRecyclingCascade.aria: A cascade of rainfall bars running inland from the coast: {rho} percent of the total rain is recycled water, and {interior} millimetres reach the deepest interior segment
moistureRecyclingCascade.worldLabel: Which world's air is making the crossing

readout.recycledNote: Share of all rainfall on this fetch
readout.costNote: Rain lost in the deep interior

verdict.intact: An unbroken forest hands its water forward, and the interior stays wet on rain it helped make.
verdict.thinning: The cleared ground returns far less water to the sky, and every stretch downwind of it gets a thinner share.
verdict.broken: The chain is cut. The deep interior is not dry because it was cleared — it is dry because its supplier was.

moistureRecyclingCascade.footnote: Each bar is the rain wrung out of the column over 500 km of fetch. The bright upper part is water a leaf sent back up; the dim lower part is vapour still on its first pass from the sea.

raindropGrowthLadder.title: Two barriers between vapour and rain
raindropGrowthLadder.subtitle: A drop must first be allowed to start, and then find a second way to grow.
raindropGrowthLadder.worldLabel: Whose gravity and air the drop is falling through

panel.kohler: Can it start? — the humidity a speck needs before a droplet runs away
panel.growth: Can it fall? — how fast the drop sinks as it grows

aria.kohler: An activation curve peaking at {sc} percent supersaturation, at a droplet radius of {rc} micrometres
aria.growth: A growth track showing diffusion stalling after {stall} minutes and coalescence carrying the drop to a fall speed of {fall} metres per second

hint.haze: Below the peak the droplet is stable haze. It swells and shrinks with the humidity and never becomes rain.
hint.activated: Past the peak no equilibrium is left. The droplet grows without limit — but growing is not yet falling.

readout.stallNote: After {min} minutes of growing, still cloud
readout.rainNote: {jump}× the volume of a cloud droplet

raindropGrowthLadder.footnote: Both panels share one ruler along the bottom, so a droplet's place on the activation curve is its place on the growth track. Pure vapour would need roughly five times saturation to nucleate unaided — which is why every raindrop on any world begins on a speck of something else.

perchedWaterBudget.title: Paying for a waterfall with fog
perchedWaterBudget.subtitle: A floating mountain has no watershed. Every litre leaving its rim was caught from the air.
perchedWaterBudget.aria: Two columns compared on a logarithmic scale: {capture} cubic metres per second captured from fog against {demand} leaving the massif

controls.venturi: Let the gaps between massifs funnel the wind (speculative)

verdict.solvent: The books close. At this discharge, fog interception alone can keep the plateau supplied.
verdict.marginal: Nearly. Fog is the right order of magnitude here, and a modest store inside the rock would cover the rest.
verdict.shortfall: Fog is real but not enough. A cataract this size needs several times the water the air is delivering.
verdict.impossible: Not close. At the discharges the films show, fog interception is short by more than an order of magnitude.

readout.sustainableNote: After the plateau forest takes its share

perchedWaterBudget.footnote: Canon shows the waterfalls and never says how big they are, so the discharge is yours to set. The dark line across each column marks its split: on the left, plateau capture beneath face impaction; on the right, the forest's own thirst beneath the visible fall.
